X.sentence: Cristina can demand the landlord to professionally remove the mold (OR Art. 259a Abs. 1), as the mold is a defect not caused by her and not her responsibility to fix.  [OR Art. 259a Abs. 1]
X.label: unsupported
X.why: Cause of mold is disputed (X1); text asserts as fact it is not caused by her.

X.sentence: If the landlord does not fix the mold, Cristina can request a proportional rent reduction from the time she learned of the defect until it is repaired (OR Art. 259d).  [OR Art. 259d]
X.label: wrong_law
X.why: Reduction is not conditional on landlord failing to fix; and 259d runs from when the LANDLORD learned of the defect, not the tenant.

X.sentence: If the mold has caused Cristina any damage (e.g., ruined belongings), she can claim compensation from the landlord, unless the landlord proves no fault (OR Art. 259e).  [OR Art. 259e]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct summary of 259e incl. reversed burden on fault; conditional on damage.

X.sentence: If the landlord continues to deny responsibility, Cristina may consider depositing the rent (OR Art. 259a Abs. 2) as a protective measure.  [OR Art. 259a Abs. 2]
X.label: ok
X.why: Deposit right exists (259a II); procedure follows in 259g section.

X.sentence: Since the landlord has not removed the mold within a reasonable time, Cristina may either have the mold professionally removed at the landlord's expense (as the mold reduces the apartment's habitability) or, if the mold completely prevents the apartment from being used as intended, Cristina may terminate the lease immediately.  [OR Art. 259b]
X.label: unsupported
X.why: Asserts landlord failed within reasonable time; only a phone report last month, no deadline set. Also narrows termination to 'completely prevents' (omits 'erheblich beeinträchtigt') and gives substitute repair without the 'not substantial' condition.

X.sentence: If it is established that the mold is caused by insufficient ventilation on Cristina's part, then the landlord would not be obligated to remove the mold under this provision.  [OR Art. 259b]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct: 259a/259b only for defects the tenant is not responsible for; relevant given disputed cause.

X.sentence: Cristina must send the landlord a written notice demanding mold removal within a reasonable timeframe and may threaten to deposit future rent payments with the cantonal authority if the landlord fails to act.  [OR Art. 259g Abs. 1]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct 259g I written deadline + threat to deposit (omits written announcement of deposit, minor).

X.sentence: If Cristina deposits the rent with the cantonal authority after the deadline passes, those rent payments will be considered paid.  [OR Art. 259g Abs. 2]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct 259g II.

X.sentence: If the landlord has not yet set a written payment deadline with a termination warning for unpaid rent, Cristina cannot yet reduce or withhold rent under OR Art. 257d Abs. 1.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 1]
X.label: wrong_law
X.why: 257d is the landlord's arrears-termination procedure; it does not govern when the tenant may reduce/withhold rent.

X.sentence: If the landlord has not yet served a proper written notice after the payment deadline passed without full payment, Cristina cannot yet terminate the lease under OR Art. 257d Abs. 2.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
X.label: wrong_law
X.why: Wrong party: 257d II lets the LANDLORD terminate; nothing about the tenant terminating.

X.sentence: If Cristina has not yet deposited rent with the Zurich conciliation authority within 30 days of the first deposit, the deposited rent belongs to the landlord under OR Art. 259h Abs. 1.  [OR Art. 259h Abs. 1]
X.label: wrong_law
X.why: Garbled: 259h I requires the tenant to bring claims before the conciliation authority within 30 days of the first deposited rent falling due; she has not deposited anything.

X.sentence: If Cristina has not yet notified the landlord of the rent deposit, the landlord could request the return of any wrongfully deposited rent from the conciliation authority under OR Art. 259h Abs. 2.  [OR Art. 259h Abs. 2]
X.label: wrong_law
X.why: Reversed: landlord can request release as soon as the tenant HAS announced the deposit.

Y.sentence: If the mold is caused by a maintenance defect the landlord is responsible for, Cristina can demand the landlord fix the mold, request a rent reduction from the date she learned of the problem, and claim compensation for any harm caused by the mold.  [OR Art. 259a Abs. 1]
Y.label: wrong_law
Y.why: Conditional on cause is good, but reduction runs from when the landlord learned of the defect (259d), not the tenant; damages ignore landlord's fault defence.

Y.sentence: If the landlord insists Cristina must clean the mold herself with vinegar, Cristina should insist on professional remediation and document all communications, as the landlord is obligated to keep the apartment habitable.  [OR Art. 256 Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Reasonable advice grounded in 256 I; documentation is useful.

Y.sentence: If Cristina decides to pay reduced rent, she should notify the landlord in writing before the next rent payment and keep copies of all correspondence, as rent reductions require clear communication.  [OR Art. 259d]
Y.label: wrong_law
Y.why: Implies unilateral rent reduction is lawful with written notice; under Swiss law reduction must be claimed/agreed or ordered, self-help deduction creates arrears (257d termination risk) — the client's stated plan.

Y.sentence: If the landlord has not fixed the mold within a reasonable time, Cristina may either have the mold removed at the landlord’s expense or, if the mold makes the apartment unfit or seriously impairs its use, she could even end the tenancy immediately.  [OR Art. 259b]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct conditional 259b (knowledge + reasonable time, termination for unfit/serious impairment).

Y.sentence: If the mold only slightly reduces the apartment’s suitability but the landlord still refuses to fix it, Cristina can demand that the landlord pay for professional mold removal.  [OR Art. 259b]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct gist of 259b lit. b (repair at landlord's cost for non-serious defect).

Y.sentence: If Cristina sends the landlord a written notice demanding professional mold removal within a reasonable time and warns that she will deposit future rents with the cantonal authority if the mold is not fixed, she can legally withhold rent payments once the deadline passes.  [OR Art. 259g Abs. 1]
Y.label: wrong_law
Y.why: 259g allows depositing future rent with the cantonal office, not withholding it; withholding = arrears. Also omits written announcement.

Y.sentence: If Cristina deposits the rent with the cantonal authority after the deadline passes, those deposits will count as paid rent until the mold is properly removed.  [OR Art. 259g Abs. 2]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 259g II.

Y.sentence: If Cristina has not yet sent a written notice to the landlord, she should do so immediately, clearly describing the mold problem, requesting professional remediation, and setting a fair deadline before considering rent reductions or deposits.  [OR Art. 259g Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Actionable, correct first step (written notice with deadline).

Y.sentence: If the landlord has not yet sent a written notice demanding payment of overdue rent with a clear deadline and warning of termination, Cristina cannot legally reduce or withhold rent based on the mold issue alone.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 1]
Y.label: wrong_law
Y.why: Mislinks 257d (landlord's arrears procedure) to the tenant's right to reduce/withhold.

Y.sentence: If the landlord has already issued a formal written payment deadline for rent and Cristina has not paid within that time, the landlord could then terminate the lease with a 30-day notice.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct conditional warning on 257d II (30 days to end of month simplified); relevant since client plans to pay less.

Y.sentence: If Cristina decides to withhold rent, she should only do so after the landlord has failed to fix the mold despite proper notice, and she should keep clear records and photos of the mold and all communications.  [OR Art. 259h Abs. 1]
Y.label: wrong_law
Y.why: Presents withholding as allowed after notice; only deposit is allowed, and 259h I requires filing with conciliation authority within 30 days — omitted.

missing_key_points.X: No warning that unilateral 30% cut risks arrears termination (257d); no 30-day filing duty after deposit stated correctly; no advice to document/send written defect notice first.
missing_key_points.Y: Unilateral reduction and 'withholding' presented as permissible; 30-day conciliation filing after deposit missing; no mention that reduction runs from landlord's knowledge.

X.sentence: If the client pays the overdue rent before the deadline in the letter expires, they can avoid the immediate risk of eviction.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 1]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct: full payment within the letter's deadline averts 257d termination.

X.sentence: If the client cannot pay the full amount by the deadline, they should immediately seek help from a legal aid office or tenants' association to explore options like negotiating a payment plan or contesting the notice.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
X.label: ok
X.why: Sound practical step; 'contesting the notice' is vague (no termination yet) but not misleading.

X.sentence: If the landlord has already sent a formal demand for payment with a threat of termination, the client must act quickly to avoid eviction.  [OR Art. 266n]
X.label: noise
X.why: Demand is a confirmed fact, so the 'if' is empty; says nothing about 266n (separate delivery to spouse).

X.sentence: If the landlord later serves notice of termination, the client should immediately seek legal advice because eviction is usually not delayed if the termination is based on unpaid rent.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 1]
X.label: ok
X.why: Roughly correct (272a I excludes extension for arrears termination; 'usually not delayed' is a soft simplification).

X.sentence: If the landlord offers an equivalent replacement apartment, the client cannot request an extension of the lease.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 2]
X.label: noise
X.why: Irrelevant hypothetical (extension already excluded for 257d termination); also overstates 272a II, which says 'in der Regel'.

Y.sentence: The landlord has already sent a written demand for payment of the overdue rent with a threat of termination, giving the client at least ten days (or more if it is an apartment) to pay the arrears.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct; '(or more if apartment)' is vague — the flat minimum is 30 days — but not wrong.

Y.sentence: If the client does not pay the overdue rent in full within the set deadline, the landlord can terminate the lease for an apartment with at least 30 days' notice.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 257d II for flats (omits 'to end of a month').

Y.sentence: If the client pays the outstanding rent before the deadline expires, the landlord cannot proceed with termination.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct consequence of timely payment.

Y.sentence: If the landlord serves a termination notice due to unpaid rent (Art. 257d), it must also be separately delivered to the client's spouse or registered partner, but this fact is currently unknown.  [OR Art. 266n]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct and flags unknown marital status; misses that 266n also covers the payment demand already received.

Y.sentence: If the landlord gives the client notice of termination for unpaid rent, the client will not be able to request an extension of the lease (Art. 272a Abs. 1).  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 272a I; important for client with children.

Y.sentence: If the landlord offers the client an equivalent replacement apartment, an extension of the lease will generally be excluded (Art. 272a Abs. 2).  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 2]
Y.label: noise
Y.why: Correct but irrelevant: extension already excluded for 257d termination.

missing_key_points.X: No concrete deadline (>=30 days, code date 2026-12-08); no mention that social assistance (Sozialhilfe) can cover arrears; no check of marital status (266n/266o nullity); consequences of non-payment (termination, no extension) only vague.
missing_key_points.Y: No action steps (pay in full, apply to social services/Sozialhilfe for arrears, get advice); concrete deadline date not given; 266n relevance to the payment demand itself missed.

X.sentence: If the client has already received a formal written notice from the landlord demanding payment of overdue rent and threatening termination, they must act quickly because the landlord can now legally proceed with eviction after the deadline passes.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct gist: after the 257d deadline lapses the landlord may terminate ('eviction' is a lay simplification).

X.sentence: If the client has not yet paid the overdue rent by the deadline set in the notice, they risk losing their flat when the notice period expires, so they should prioritize paying the arrears or contacting the landlord immediately to discuss a payment plan.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct risk and sensible action; payment plan only helps if landlord agrees (not stated, minor).

X.sentence: If the client has not yet picked up or fully understood the letter, they should immediately collect and read the notice carefully to confirm the deadline and amount owed before deciding on their next steps.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 1]
X.label: ok
X.why: Useful step (confirm deadline and amount); he has picked it up, but reading carefully still applies.

X.sentence: If Luca moves out or hands back the flat before the eviction process is completed, he could then propose a suitable replacement tenant to avoid paying rent until the lease ends.  [OR Art. 264 Abs. 1]

X.sentence: If Luca does not move out or return the flat, he must pay the rent until the lease legally ends, as he cannot use the replacement-tenant option to avoid payment.  [OR Art. 264 Abs. 2]
X.label: noise
X.why: Muddled use of 264 II (which concerns early return without replacement); trivially true but useless.

X.sentence: If the landlord has already sent a formal notice of termination due to unpaid rent, the law generally does not allow an extension of the lease, so Luca cannot rely on a legal stay extension to avoid eviction.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 1]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct 272a I: no extension after arrears termination.

X.sentence: If the landlord offers Luca an equivalent alternative place to live, the law would normally bar any extension of his current tenancy.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 2]
X.label: noise
X.why: Irrelevant hypothetical (272a II).

X.sentence: If Luca does not pay the overdue rent by the deadline in the letter, the landlord could legally proceed with eviction, so he should act quickly to either pay the arrears or negotiate a payment plan with the property management.  [OR Art. 257d]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct and actionable; repeats sentence 2.

Y.sentence: Since you received a formal notice from the landlord with a payment deadline and threat of termination, the landlord can now proceed to terminate the tenancy if you do not pay the overdue rent within the required period.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 257d I consequence.

Y.sentence: If the payment deadline set by the landlord in the notice has passed without full payment, the landlord can terminate the tenancy for your flat with at least 30 days' notice.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 257d II for flats (omits 'end of a month').

Y.sentence: If you pay the outstanding rent before the landlord issues the formal termination notice, the eviction process will be stopped.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
Y.label: wrong_law
Y.why: Wrong cut-off: only full payment WITHIN the set deadline prevents termination; paying later but before the termination notice does not. Dangerous for a client who wants to wait until month-end pay.

Y.sentence: If Luca moves out or hands back the flat before paying the rent, he must either propose a suitable replacement tenant or continue paying rent until the lease ends.  [OR Art. 264 Abs. 1]
Y.label: noise
Y.why: 264 I gist correct but irrelevant (no move-out plan); 'before paying the rent' is confused.

Y.sentence: If Luca does not move out or hand back the flat, he must continue paying rent until the lease ends or a legal termination is possible.  [OR Art. 264 Abs. 2]
Y.label: noise
Y.why: Correct but irrelevant 264 II restatement.

Y.sentence: If Luca moves out or hands back the flat, the landlord must account for any savings or gains from the flat during that time.  [OR Art. 264 Abs. 3]
Y.label: noise
Y.why: Correct gist of 264 III but irrelevant.

Y.sentence: If the landlord has given notice of termination due to unpaid rent (Art. 257d), the law excludes any extension of the lease, so Luca cannot request an extension.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 272a I.

Y.sentence: If the landlord offers Luca an equivalent replacement flat, the law generally excludes an extension even if he is a young employee in Zurich.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 2]
Y.label: noise
Y.why: Irrelevant hypothetical with odd 'young employee' remark.

Y.sentence: If the landlord has not yet served a formal termination notice, these rules do not yet apply to Luca's situation.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct clarification that 272a is not yet triggered.

missing_key_points.X: No concrete deadline (period >=30 days; code earliest 2026-11-25) and no warning that month-end pay may come too late; no point that only FULL payment counts; no mention of father/social services as source of funds; non-collection of registered letter does not delay receipt.
missing_key_points.Y: Misstates the payment cut-off; no deadline date; no action steps (pay in full, accept father's help or social services); 264 material crowds out key points.

X.sentence: If the landlord has not legally asserted any claim against Sandro within one year of the lease ending, Sandro can ask the bank to return the deposit.  [OR Art. 257e Abs. 3]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct 257e III.

X.sentence: If the landlord continues to refuse to sign or communicate, Sandro should document all attempts to resolve the issue and consider contacting the bank directly to request the deposit based on the one-year rule.  [OR Art. 257e Abs. 3]
X.label: inapplicable
X.why: Suggests asking the bank now 'based on the one-year rule', but only 4 of 12 months have passed; the bank cannot release on that basis yet.

X.sentence: If the landlord still does not respond after one year from Sandro’s move-out, Sandro can proceed with the bank to get the deposit back without the landlord’s signature.  [OR Art. 257e Abs. 3]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct (one year without a legally asserted claim); 'does not respond' is a loose paraphrase.

X.sentence: If the landlord refuses to sign the release form, the bank will likely not release the deposit without his signature.  [OR Art. 267a Abs. 1]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct practical consequence of 257e III (cited to 267a).

X.sentence: If the landlord does not respond to emails or complete the handover process, he may lose his right to claim any deductions from the deposit.  [OR Art. 267a Abs. 2]
X.label: ok
X.why: Hedged but correct gist of 267a II (claims for detectable defects lost without prompt inspection/notice).

X.sentence: If the landlord later claims there are hidden damages that were not obvious during the handover, he must notify Sandro immediately to avoid losing his right to claim them.  [OR Art. 267a Abs. 3]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct 267a III.

Y.sentence: Since Sandro moved out four months ago, if the landlord has not legally asserted any claim against him within one year, Sandro can demand the bank return the security deposit.  [OR Art. 257e Abs. 3]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct conditional; does not spell out that ~8 months remain.

Y.sentence: If the landlord has not yet legally asserted any claim against Sandro within one year of the lease ending, Sandro can request the bank to release the deposit.  [OR Art. 257e Abs. 3]
Y.label: noise
Y.why: Duplicate of the previous sentence.

Y.sentence: According to OR Art. 267a Abs. 1, the landlord must inspect the flat upon return and immediately notify Sandro of any defects he is responsible for.  [OR Art. 267a Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 267a I.

Y.sentence: If the landlord fails to inspect the flat and report defects as required, he loses his claims against Sandro, unless the defects were not detectable during a proper inspection.  [OR Art. 267a Abs. 2]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 267a II.

Y.sentence: If the landlord later discovers defects that were not initially detectable, he must immediately notify Sandro.  [OR Art. 267a Abs. 3]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Correct 267a III.

missing_key_points.X: Does not say the one-year release date is ~8 months away, nor that Sandro can go to the conciliation authority now to obtain release; does not apply 267a to the 'handover was fine' fact as a reason the landlord likely lost claims; no written demand step.
missing_key_points.Y: Pure law restatement: no application to Sandro (handover fine -> likely no claims for visible defects), no date when one year runs out, no next step (registered demand letter, conciliation authority).

X.sentence: If the rental agreement or house rules prohibit pets without an explicit exception for mental support animals, this prohibition may be invalid under OR Art. 256 Abs. 2 because it is a pre-formulated rule disadvantaging the tenant.  [OR Art. 256 Abs. 2]
X.label: wrong_law
X.why: 256 II only voids deviations from the landlord's maintenance duty (256 I); it does not invalidate pet bans, and the 'mental support animal exception' condition is invented.

X.sentence: Greta must use her flat carefully and consider her neighbours, including respecting house rules that prohibit pets.  [OR Art. 257f Abs. 1]
X.label: unsupported
X.why: 257f says nothing about pets; asserts the house-rule ban binds her although it is unknown whether it is part of her 25-year-old contract.

X.sentence: If Greta continues to keep the cat despite the property management’s written warning after violating the pet ban, the landlord could terminate the lease with at least 30 days’ notice.  [OR Art. 257f Abs. 3]
X.label: ok
X.why: Gist of 257f III correct (omits 'unreasonable to continue' and 'end of a month'); relevant risk warning.

X.sentence: If the property management intends to unilaterally change the contract to prohibit pets, they must use the approved form and provide a valid reason.  [OR Art. 269d Abs. 3]
X.label: ok
X.why: Correct and key: a newly imposed ban in a 25-year tenancy is a unilateral change needing the 269d form and reasons.

Y.sentence: If the property management’s house rules ban pets, this clause may be invalid if it is part of pre‑printed terms or the rental agreement itself.  [OR Art. 256 Abs. 2]
Y.label: wrong_law
Y.why: Inverted: a ban in the contract itself is what makes it binding; 256 II does not void pet clauses.

Y.sentence: If Greta can show the cat is necessary for her mental well‑being, she may be able to request an exception to the pet ban.  [OR Art. 256 Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Practical (she may ask); weak legal basis in 256 I, but phrased as a request, not a right.

Y.sentence: If no formal notice has been sent yet, Greta should ask the management to put any pet ban in writing and note the date, so she can check whether the rule is enforceable.  [OR Art. 256 Abs. 1]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Reasonable step to clarify the source/date of the rule.

Y.sentence: If no written warning has been issued yet, Greta should ask the property management in writing to reconsider the pet ban, explaining the emotional support the cat would provide after her husband’s death.  [OR Art. 257f Abs. 2]
Y.label: ok
Y.why: Practical, relevant next step.

missing_key_points.X: Key check not spelled out: was the pet ban part of the contract/house rules she signed 25 years ago? If not, a new ban is void without the 269d form. No advice to wait before taking the cat.
missing_key_points.Y: Misses the 269d point (unilateral change needs official form, otherwise void) and the 257f III termination risk if she takes the cat against a valid ban; no 'check the original contract' step.

X.sentence: The landlord must have notified the rent increase on an approved form at least ten days before the notice period began and provided a valid reason; if not, the increase is invalid (OR Art. 269d Abs. 2).  [OR Art. 269d Abs. 2]
X.label: ok

X.sentence: Maria can contest the rent increase as abusive within 30 days of receiving the notice at the Zurich conciliation authority (OR Art. 270b Abs. 1).  [OR Art. 270b Abs. 1]
X.label: ok
X.why: Key point, correct: 30 days from receipt to challenge at the conciliation authority (270b I).

X.sentence: If Maria can prove the rent increase results in an excessive return for the landlord due to cost reductions, she can demand a reduction in rent in writing to the landlord within 30 days (OR Art. 270a Abs. 2).  [OR Art. 270a Abs. 2]
X.label: wrong_law
X.why: 270a II: the landlord (not Maria) has 30 days to respond; 270a reduction for cost reductions is not the route against a fresh increase.

X.sentence: If Maria wishes to challenge the increase and request a reduction simultaneously, she must do so in one written request to avoid the 30-day separate procedure (OR Art. 270a Abs. 3).  [OR Art. 270a Abs. 3]

X.sentence: If the landlord has not yet sent a written notice to Maria setting a payment deadline and warning of termination for the rent increase, then the law does not yet require Maria to face an immediate termination threat.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 1]

X.sentence: If the landlord has not yet sent a written notice to Maria setting a payment deadline and warning of termination for the rent increase, then Maria would only need to worry about termination if the landlord later sends such a notice and she fails to pay within the deadline.  [OR Art. 257d Abs. 2]
X.label: noise
X.why: Irrelevant arrears hypothetical; also ignores that other termination routes exist.

X.sentence: If the landlord has given notice of termination of the lease, the law would exclude any extension of the tenancy under OR Art. 272a Abs. 1 because no such termination notice has been given yet.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 1]

X.sentence: If the landlord offers Maria a substitute accommodation of equal value, the law would generally exclude an extension under OR Art. 272a Abs. 2, but no such offer has been made.  [OR Art. 272a Abs. 2]

X.sentence: If Maria cannot obtain her husband's consent or it is unreasonably refused, she can apply to the judge for assistance.  [OR Art. 266m Abs. 2]

Y.sentence: If Maria believes the new rent is too high because it would give the landlord an excessive profit, she can ask the landlord to lower it in writing and, if he does not agree, take the matter to the Zurich mediation authority.  [OR Art. 270a Abs. 1]
